text:
jia: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector patch we saw a perf cliff in TP all-reduce for message sizes ~16-64KB. Repro on 8xA100, model: gpt-6B-ish config. Root latency for reduce step jumped ~1.8x at 32KB. Profiling attached below.

sam: ugh. did selector start preferring tree for those sizes?

jia: yes, selector rule now picks 'tree' if avg-msg < 48KB to avoid ring handshake overhead. But likely we misestimated kernel cost for fragments vs unity.

dmitri: can you paste the perf logs? Also which NCCL version?

jia: nccl 2.14.4, runtime build af0f. here's simplified nvprof timeline (only all-reduce):
```
msg_size bytes | ring ms | tree ms
8KB           | 0.9     | 1.0
16KB          | 1.1     | 1.05
32KB          | 1.3     | 2.4   <-- big regression
64KB          | 1.6     | 2.1
128KB         | 2.0     | 2.2
```

jia: ring stays linear while tree spikes around 32KB — suggests tree's fanout + handshake cost dominates at these mid sizes, perhaps due to our chunking aligning to 32KB boundaries and causing extra fragments.

erin: do we have KV cache/fragment alignment involved? recent kvcache coalesce change adjusted max-frag to 32KB right?

jia: yes — coalesce now pads to 32KB in some paths. That could bump many messages over threshold causing tree selection to hit bad region.

sam: maybe selector should use post-coalesce size not pre-coalesce. Or add a hysteresis to avoid flipping at boundary.

dmitri: agree. Also kernel measurement should include end-to-end with kv cache enabled since that changes effective msg distribution.

perf-bot: perf/regression @jia compared to baseline 2955400000: +42% reduce latency at 32KB, CI flagged.

erin: can someone run microbench that sweeps msg sizes 8K-128K with kv-cache on/off and selector forced ring/tree? I'll run with 8 GPUs later tonight.

sam: i'll adjust selector to prefer ring up to 48KB and add an opt-in flag to test. quick patch:
```
if (post_coalesce_size <= 48KB) prefer = RING;
else if (post_coalesce_size >= 96KB) prefer = TREE;
else prefer = auto_tune();
```

jia: sweet. also logging: add histogram of post_coalesce_size to per-model metrics so we can tune in prod.

dmitri: one more thought — kernel autoswitch had an assumption about contiguous msgbuffers. If coalesce introduces padding, effective kernel copy cost increases. Add copy accounting.

jia: noted. I'll create a repro script and attach a flamegraph. For now, temporary mitigation = selector change + revert padding to 16KB for kvcache.

erin: :thumbsup: thanks. keep this in the incident channel if it impacts hosted customers.

sam: opened PR 4723 w/ ring bias + log; marking as draft.

jia: thanks all — will post results once the nightly sweep completes.
